# Phase 01.1 Plan 10: Dashboard, Venue Switcher and Venue Surfaces Summary

**Nine owner-surface files re-skinned onto the Cena system at the 44px touch floor, with the sidebar collapsing rather than shrinking on a phone, the last three 50%-alpha focus rings in the repo retired, and every glyph routed through the `Icon` wrapper.**

## Performance

- **Duration:** 22 min
- **Started:** 2026-08-05T02:39:00Z
- **Completed:** 2026-08-05T03:01:00Z
- **Tasks:** 3
- **Files modified:** 9

## Accomplishments

- **The sidebar now collapses instead of shrinking.** Below `md` the shell's `w-56` column ate 224px of a 320px viewport and left the content region 96px wide. It is now a full-width band above the content, dropping `sticky`, `h-dvh`, `w-56` and its own scroll container. This is the single largest SC3 ("usable one-handed on a phone") change in the plan.
- **Every interactive row on these surfaces meets the 44px floor**, taken as `min-h-11` on the row rather than by inflating padding — nav rows, the create-venue link, the switcher trigger, and both native dropdown controls (which shipped at `h-9`/36px).
- **The last three `ring-ring/50` call sites in the repo are gone.** All 19 primitives already wrote the contract's `ring-ring/30`; these three surface call sites were the remainder. `grep -rn "ring-ring/50" app components` now returns nothing.
- **Two keyboard-focus gaps closed** (Rule 2): the create-venue sidebar link and the dashboard nav rows had no focus treatment at all, so a keyboard owner tabbing the sidebar could not see where they were.
- **A real overflow defect found and fixed** in the switcher dropdown — see Deviations.
- All glyphs on the nine files draw through the `Icon` wrapper at 1.75 stroke; no raw lucide JSX element remains on any of them.

## Task Commits

Each task was committed atomically:

1. **Task 1: Re-skin the dashboard shell — layout, nav and error boundary** — `6a9a778` (feat)
2. **Task 2: Re-skin the venue switcher across its server/client split** — `020497f` (feat)
3. **Task 3: Re-skin the three venue pages and the venue form** — `fd60238` (feat)

## Files Created/Modified

- `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` — Sidebar collapses to a band below `md`; wordmark to the Display role in `--font-serif`; create-venue link gains the 44px floor and the 30% accent ring; `Plus` routed through `Icon`. The create-venue link stays unconditional and the staff-and-device gate block is byte-identical.
- `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` — Page title to Display; 24px padding stepping to the 32px desktop margin; card bounded to a readable measure. Copy unchanged.
- `components/dashboard-nav.tsx` — Rows at 44px with the accent focus ring; horizontal scrolling band on mobile; all four glyphs through `Icon`; the map's `icon: Icon` binding renamed `Glyph` so it no longer shadows the wrapper.
- `app/(dashboard)/components/VenueSwitcher.tsx` — Comment only. The Supabase read, the below-two-venues threshold and the server/client split are untouched.
- `app/(dashboard)/components/venue-switcher-menu.tsx` — Trigger at 44px with the 30% ring; dropdown height doubly bounded; both glyphs through `Icon`; currency chip composes `Badge`.
- `app/(dashboard)/venues/page.tsx` — 24px→32px page padding on the shared creation wrapper.
- `app/(dashboard)/venues/new/page.tsx` — The same wrapper, kept byte-for-byte identical to its sibling.
- `app/(dashboard)/venues/[venueId]/page.tsx` — Venue name to Display; header wraps at 320px instead of clipping; currency chip composes `Badge`; details list stacks to one column at 320px.
- `components/venue-form.tsx` — Both native dropdown controls retained and given the Cena input treatment (control-border boundary, paper fill, Body role, 44px floor, 30% ring); `Loader2` through `Icon`. The language-checkbox block and `lib/copy.ts` are untouched.

## Decisions Made

- **`dashboard-nav.tsx` stays a Client Component.** See Deviations 1 — the plan's premise about it was factually wrong.
- **The switcher dropdown's height is bounded by a `min()` of a fixed ceiling and Radix's measured available height**, because the two caps are in the same twMerge group and only one can survive.
- **Currency chips compose the `Badge` primitive** in both the venue header and the switcher row. They render the same value for the same venue, so two hand-rolled spans of differing shape would read as two systems.
- **The venue details list stacks to one column below `sm`.** The `[auto_1fr]` grid left the value column roughly 150px wide on a phone, enough to wrap `Europe/Bucharest` mid-word.
- **Contract comments on all nine files re-pointed at `01.1-UI-SPEC.md`** (and its E12 element id) per the phase's stated convention; several still cited the superseded `01-UI-SPEC.md` E4/E5 sections.

## Deviations from Plan

### Auto-fixed Issues

**1. [Rule 3 - Blocking] `components/dashboard-nav.tsx` is a Client Component, not a Server Component**

- **Found during:** Task 1
- **Issue:** The plan's `read_first` ("it is a Server Component today"), its acceptance criterion (`grep -c '"use client"' … components/dashboard-nav.tsx` returns 0), its action ("Keep it a Server Component") and `01.1-PATTERNS.md` § "Server/client split" all assert this file is server-rendered. It has carried `"use client"` since it was written, and its own header comment says so: it reads `usePathname()` to mark the active nav row. Converting it would not merely lose the accent the plan requires on that row — it would fail the build, because `usePathname` is a client hook.
- **Fix:** Left it a Client Component and documented the reasoning in the file header, distinguishing it from the rule it appears to breach: the "do not push a Server Component to the client" rule exists to keep a **Supabase read** off the browser, and this file performs none. It *is* the sanctioned shape — the interactive leaf in its own client component, exactly as `VenueSwitcher` (server, does the read) → `venue-switcher-menu` (client, holds the interaction) is. The two files the threat register actually names, `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and `VenueSwitcher.tsx`, both remain Server Components and both were verified at 0 occurrences.
- **Files modified:** `components/dashboard-nav.tsx`
- **Verification:** `grep -c '"use client"' 'app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx'` → 0; same for `VenueSwitcher.tsx` → 0. `pnpm build` exit 0. T-01.1-30 holds.
- **Committed in:** `6a9a778`

**2. [Rule 1 - Bug] The switcher dropdown could grow to the full height of the smallest supported viewport**

- **Found during:** Task 2
- **Issue:** The dropdown carried `max-h-80` at the call site while the re-skinned primitive carries `max-h-(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height)`. Both are `max-h-*`, so twMerge kept the call site's literal and **dropped the primitive's cap**. 320px is the entire height of the smallest viewport this phase targets, so the menu could fill the screen edge-to-edge — precisely the case the plan's overflow backstop is about ("scrolls within its own container at 320px rather than growing past the viewport").
- **Fix:** Replaced with `max-h-[min(20rem,var(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height))]` — one utility, so nothing is dropped, and the menu is bounded by both a fixed ceiling and the room Radix measured between the trigger and the viewport edge.
- **Files modified:** `app/(dashboard)/components/venue-switcher-menu.tsx`
- **Verification:** `pnpm exec vitest run tests/lib/create-venue-affordance.test.tsx` green, including its assertion that the create item stays inside the menu's scroll container. Full suite green. Visual confirmation is deliverable D8 (backstop).
- **Committed in:** `020497f`

**3. [Rule 2 - Missing Critical] No keyboard focus indicator on the sidebar's interactive rows**

- **Found during:** Task 1
- **Issue:** The create-venue link and all four dashboard nav rows had `hover:` treatment but no `focus-visible:` treatment whatsoever. A keyboard owner tabbing through the sidebar had no indication of where focus sat. The contract lists the focus ring as one of the closed set of places the accent is permitted, so its absence was an omission rather than a choice.
- **Fix:** Added the system's standard 3px accent ring at 30% alpha (`focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/30` with `outline-none`) to both, matching what all 19 primitives write.
- **Files modified:** `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`, `components/dashboard-nav.tsx`
- **Verification:** `pnpm build` exit 0; full suite green. Visual confirmation is part of D7.
- **Committed in:** `6a9a778`

### Acceptance criteria that were factually unsatisfiable

These are recorded rather than worked around. No source was contorted to make a grep pass.

**4. `grep -c 'COPY.venues.createAnotherHeading' components/venue-form.tsx` returns at least 1**

- **Found during:** Task 3
- **Finding:** All four venue copy rows were **already wired by plan 01.1-03** before this plan started. `venue-form.tsx` reads `COPY.venues.createFirstHeading` / `createFirstBody` as its prop defaults, and `app/(dashboard)/venues/new/page.tsx` passes `COPY.venues.createAnotherHeading` / `createAnotherBody` at the call site. The `createAnother*` pair belongs at the call site — it is the add-another *screen's* wording, and a component whose defaults are the first-venue wording has no reason to name it. Satisfying the criterion literally would have required inventing a dead reference.
- **Resolution:** Left as-is. The criterion's actual intent — the plan's must_have "the four venue copy rows are read from the copy deck rather than from a hardcoded default prop" — is satisfied across the pair of files. `grep -c 'Add your first venue' components/venue-form.tsx` returns 0 and `git diff lib/copy.ts` is empty, both as the plan requires.

**5. `grep -c '<select' components/venue-form.tsx` returns 2**

- **Found during:** Task 3
- **Finding:** `grep -c` counts matching *lines*, not elements. At the plan's own base commit this returned **3**: two real elements plus one mention inside the WR-08 rationale comment, which sits in the block this plan is forbidden to touch. The criterion was off by one before execution began.
- **Resolution:** Both native controls survive and are confirmed by line number (152 and 206, plus the pre-existing comment at line 97). My own new contract comment initially added a fourth match by naming the tag in prose; per the phase's known trap — a contract comment quoting the form it discusses tripping the very grep that measures it — the comment was rewritten to *describe* the element instead, returning the count to its baseline 3. `grep -c 'from "@/components/ui/select"'` returns 0, confirming the registry listbox was not swapped in.

---

**Total deviations:** 3 auto-fixed (1 blocking, 1 bug, 1 missing critical) + 2 unsatisfiable acceptance criteria recorded.
**Impact on plan:** No scope creep. All three auto-fixes were necessary for correctness or accessibility, and each is confined to a file this plan already owns. The two unsatisfiable criteria are defects in the plan text, not in the implementation — the underlying must_haves they were meant to enforce all hold.

## Issues Encountered

- **`build-assets.test.ts` fails on a fresh worktree until `pnpm build` has run.** The baseline suite reported 5 failures across 1 file before any edit, all with the diagnosis "Run `pnpm build` first, then re-run this test." This is an environment precondition, not a regression. After the first build, the suite is 728/728 green and stayed there through all three tasks.
- **One transient failure on the final suite run**, in one of the two known-flaky files that hit the live local Postgres. Clean on immediate re-run (728/728), consistent with the standing guidance to re-run before treating a failure in those two files as real. All other runs in this session were green first time.
